title: River Review logical Agent Contract
description: Runtime-independent definition of WHO is responsible for a piece of review judgment (#2014, Epic #2011). Skill = what to judge, Agent = who is responsible, Flow = when/how judgment is executed. A logical Agent is NOT a Claude native subagent: a runtime that has no equivalent primitive still conforms as long as it satisfies this contract, so this document carries no host, model, or prompt vocabulary. Runtime binding lives in a separate document (`schemas/agent-adapter-map.schema.json`) precisely so an adapter difference cannot leak into judgment. Not to be confused with `agents/spec/agent.schema.json`, which describes an "AI Agent Knowledge Pack" and is a different field system. Vocabulary is closed: `id`, `responsibilities`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `capabilities` and `onUnavailable` are enums and every object sets `additionalProperties: false`, so an unknown or misspelled agent fails validation at load time instead of being silently skipped. That matches the repository-wide fail-safe direction recorded in `src/lib/gate-decision.mjs` (everything unknown or undetermined maps to the safe side).

version.description: Semantic version of this Agent Contract as a versioned asset, following the `packs:`/`skills:` convention (`schemas/pack.schema.json`). This is an asset version, not an artifact `schemaVersion`. The same `id` + `version` MUST mean the same responsibilities, inputs, outputs and authority on every runtime.

responsibilities.description: What this Agent is answerable for. Each value is owned by exactly one Agent; the non-overlap requirement (#2014 acceptance criterion) is a cross-document constraint that JSON Schema cannot express, so `tests/agent-contract.test.mjs` enforces it over the contracts in `agents/contracts/`.

inputs.description: Artifact kinds this Agent may consume. Declarative only: an Agent may not consume an artifact kind it does not declare.

outputs.description: Artifact kinds this Agent produces. These are Agent-level products; a Flow's `outputs` (#2013) are the Flow-level artifacts they feed.

skills.description: Allowed review skills, by skill id. Every id MUST already exist as an entry in `skills/registry.yaml` or as a directory under `skills/agent-skills/`; `tests/agent-contract.test.mjs` enforces that, so a contract cannot name a skill the repository does not ship. An empty array is meaningful: it declares that the Agent's judgment is deterministic and needs no skill (the case for `finding-verifier`, implemented rule-based in `src/lib/verifier.mjs`).

capabilities.description: Tool capabilities this Agent requires, named in runtime-neutral terms. Every value MUST be provided by every runtime in `agents/contracts/adapter-map.json`; the test pins the required set to the intersection of the runtimes, which is how the acceptance criterion "a Claude/Codex adapter difference must not leak into a judgment difference" is mechanized rather than asserted. Absent means the empty set.

authority.description: What this Agent is NOT allowed to do. Every field is `const: false`, so the acceptance criterion "no merge / release / policy rewrite authority" is enforced by validation and cannot be granted by editing a contract. Raising any of these requires a schema change, which is a reviewable event. This formalizes existing repository practice: the review agent declares no write tools (`agents/river-review.md`), the `auto-approve` verdict is documented as not a delegation of merge authority (`pages/reference/output-format-yaml.en.md`), and gate configuration under `.river/**` escalates unconditionally so a gate cannot switch itself off (`src/lib/gate-decision.mjs`, bootstrap cliff rule 0).

canModifySource.description: Agents review; they never write the source under review.

canApproveMerge.description: Merge stays with the host. River Review derives a gate decision; executing it is the host's responsibility (`src/lib/gate-decision.mjs`).

canRewritePolicy.description: An Agent may not edit the policy it is judged by (`.river/**`, `skills/**`, `docs/review/**`).

instantiatedPer.description: Declares that one logical Agent is instantiated once per member of an existing ledger, instead of being split into several Agents. `reviewer-role` means the keys of `REVIEWER_ROLES` in `src/lib/reviewer-orchestrator.mjs`; the ledger is deliberately NOT copied into this schema, and `tests/agent-contract.test.mjs` pins it by importing the module. This is how a lens axis stays out of the Agent axis: adding a reviewer lens does not add an Agent (see the proliferation rule in `docs/development/agent-contract.md`).

onUnavailable.description: What a runtime does when this Agent cannot run (its adapter binding is missing, or the runtime cannot provide a required capability). Both outcomes are safe-side and neither is "continue silently": `stop` halts the Flow, `escalate` hands the judgment to a human. Absent means `escalate`. There is deliberately no value that lets a run proceed as if the Agent had produced its output (#2014 unknown/missing agent fail-safe).

implementedBy.description: Where the responsibility already lives in this repository, so the contract records a mapping instead of implying new code. Every `path` must exist and every `symbol` must appear in that file; `tests/agent-contract.test.mjs` enforces both, so a stale or invented reference fails.

agentId.description: The complete logical Agent ledger. The enum is closed on purpose: Epic #2011 limits the initial set to these five, so adding a sixth is a schema change rather than a new file. A reviewer lens role (`REVIEWER_ROLES`) is a different axis and MUST NOT appear here; #2013's Flow schema reserves the `agent:` step key for exactly this vocabulary.

responsibility.description: Responsibility verbs. Names existing capability rather than new behaviour, and each verb is owned by exactly one Agent.

capability.description: Runtime-neutral tool capability names. Read-only by construction: there is no write capability to declare, which keeps `authority.canModifySource: false` consistent with what a runtime can hand the Agent.
